1	"""Core service surface for StreamMill.
2	
3	The frozen baseline only reports process health; that surface stays
4	unchanged. On top of it this module now implements named event-time
5	tumbling windows with explicit watermarks:
6	
7	* streams are created with a positive ``window_ms`` and a non-negative
8	  ``allowed_lateness_ms``;
9	* events carry an integer ``timestamp_ms`` and a finite numeric ``value``
10	  and land in the left-closed, right-open window
11	  ``[floor(timestamp_ms / window_ms) * window_ms, +window_ms)``;
12	* a per-stream watermark only moves forward; once it reaches
13	  ``window_end_ms + allowed_lateness_ms`` the window is final, is
14	  emitted exactly once, and is retained for queries;
15	* events with ``timestamp_ms < watermark - allowed_lateness_ms`` are
16	  acknowledged but dropped without touching the aggregates.
17	
18	Streams may optionally be created with a positive ``slide_ms`` (no
19	larger than ``window_ms`` and dividing it evenly). Such streams use
20	fixed-step overlapping sliding windows: an accepted event at timestamp
21	``t`` is counted once in every window ``[start, start + window_ms)``
22	whose ``start`` is an integer multiple of ``slide_ms`` and satisfies
23	``start <= t < start + window_ms`` (negative timestamps follow the same
24	mathematical grid). Every window still finalizes independently once the
25	watermark reaches its own ``window_end_ms + allowed_lateness_ms`` and is
26	emitted exactly once, ordered by window start. Without ``slide_ms`` the
27	stream is the plain tumbling stream above and every public shape is
28	unchanged.
29	
30	Streams may optionally enable event-id deduplication by passing a
31	positive ``dedup_retention_ms`` (no smaller than ``allowed_lateness_ms``)
32	at creation time. On such streams every event must carry a non-empty
33	string ``event_id``:
34	
35	* the first occurrence of an id is aggregated and remembered together
36	  with its ``timestamp_ms`` and ``value``;
37	* an exact retry (same ``timestamp_ms`` and numerically equal ``value``)
38	  is reported as ``duplicate: true`` and never touches the aggregates —
39	  the dedup check runs before the lateness check, so retained retries
40	  are duplicates even past the lateness horizon;
41	* the same id with a different timestamp or value is rejected with
42	  ``event_id_conflict`` and leaves all state untouched;
43	* an unseen id that arrives too late is dropped as usual and its id is
44	  not remembered.
45	
46	Remembered ids are evicted once the watermark advances past
47	``timestamp_ms + dedup_retention_ms`` (ids exactly on the boundary are
48	kept); evicted ids may be reused and are treated as new events.
49	
50	Streams created with a non-negative ``auto_watermark_lag_ms`` track the
51	maximum ``timestamp_ms`` of every successfully accepted event. After an
52	event is aggregated (and its id registered, when deduplicating) the
53	watermark advances atomically to
54	``max(current_watermark, max_event_timestamp - auto_watermark_lag_ms)``;
55	the lateness/dedup decision for that event uses the watermark as it was
56	before the advance. Dropped, duplicate or conflicting events never move
57	the maximum event timestamp or the watermark. Manual watermark posts keep
58	working on automatic streams and subsequent automatic advances never
59	regress below a manual watermark. Event responses on automatic streams
60	additionally carry the post-processing ``watermark_ms`` (``null`` until a
61	watermark exists) and the windows finalized by that response.
62	
63	A portable full-state snapshot is available through
64	``Service.snapshot`` / ``Service.restore_snapshot``: export produces a
65	self-contained JSON document (``format_version`` 1) capturing config,
66	watermark, open windows, finalized results and retained dedup records;
67	automatic streams additionally carry ``auto_watermark_lag_ms`` and
68	``max_event_timestamp_ms``; sliding streams additionally carry
69	``slide_ms`` (a document without it restores as a tumbling stream).
70	Restore is only accepted on an instance
71	without any streams, validates the document strictly (never silently
72	repairing it) and publishes the whole state atomically.
73	
74	In-process dimension tables provide the lookup side of an optional
75	current-value stream-table join:
76	
77	* ``POST /tables`` creates a named table; rows are written with
78	  ``PUT``-style upserts of non-empty string ``key``/``label`` pairs and
79	  report whether the stored label actually ``changed``;
80	* a stream may be created with ``lookup_table`` naming an existing
81	  table. Events on such a stream must carry a non-empty ``lookup_key``;
82	  after the usual dedup and lateness decisions the current label is read
83	  atomically (an unknown key is rejected with ``lookup_key_not_found``
84	  and leaves all state untouched) and the event is aggregated both into
85	  the plain windows and into per-window ``(lookup_key, label)`` groups.
86	  Later table writes only affect later events. Dedup records on joined
87	  streams include the ``lookup_key``, so resubmitting an id with a
88	  different key is an ``event_id_conflict``;
89	* joined groups finalize together with their window and are exposed
90	  through ``Service.joined_results``, ordered by window start, lookup
91	  key and label.
92	
93	Snapshots export as ``format_version`` 2 (adding ``tables`` plus
94	``lookup_table``/``joined_windows``/``joined_finalized`` on joined
95	streams) whenever any table exists, and restore stays compatible with
96	version 1 documents. When the join is unused every public shape and the
97	version 1 snapshot are unchanged.
98	
99	Streams may optionally materialize a window change feed by passing a
100	positive ``change_retention`` at creation time (echoed in the create
101	response; without it the stream behaves exactly as before). On such
102	streams every state change is published as a totally ordered sequence of
103	records, numbered by a ``seq`` that starts at 1 and never regresses:
104	
105	* every successfully aggregated event appends one ``upsert`` record per
106	  affected base window (ascending by window start on sliding streams),
107	  carrying the post-event ``count``/``sum`` of that window;
108	* every watermark advance that finalizes windows appends one ``final``
109	  record per newly finalized window (ascending by window start) with the
110	  final aggregates — on automatic streams the upserts of the triggering
111	  event always precede the finals of the resulting advance, and an
112	  advance without newly finalized windows appends nothing;
113	* duplicates, too-late drops, conflicts, unknown lookup keys and
114	  validation failures never consume a sequence number, and joined
115	  streams publish only the base-window changes.
116	
117	``Service.changes`` returns the retained records with ``seq`` greater
118	than a cursor, ascending, together with the current ``latest_seq``.
119	Only the newest ``change_retention`` records are kept (older ones are
120	trimmed after every commit, without moving ``latest_seq``); a cursor
121	past ``latest_seq`` raises ChangeCursorAheadError and a cursor that has
122	fallen behind the oldest retained record raises
123	ChangeCursorExpiredError.
124	
125	Instances with at least one change-feed stream export snapshots as
126	``format_version`` 3, which always carries the ``tables`` array and, on
127	enabled streams, ``change_retention``/``latest_seq``/``changes``.
128	Restore validates the retained records strictly (sequence continuity
129	against ``latest_seq`` and the retention cap, ordering, window
130	alignment, and the last retained record of every window against the
131	aggregated state) and publishes the feed so the cursor and the next
132	sequence number continue exactly as on the uninterrupted instance.
133	Version 1 and 2 documents restore as before, and instances without a
134	change feed keep exporting their original versions and shapes.
135	
136	Streams may optionally enable recoverable atomic batch ingestion by
137	passing a positive ``batch_retention`` at creation time (echoed in the
138	create response; without it the stream behaves exactly as before and the
139	batch entry point raises BatchIngestNotEnabledError). On such streams
140	``Service.add_batch`` accepts a non-empty ``batch_id`` plus 1 to 1000
141	events that each follow the stream's single-event rules:
142	
143	* the whole batch is applied at one consistent point, in input order and
144	  under the service lock, reusing the per-event dedup, lateness, lookup,
145	  window, automatic-watermark, finalization and change-feed semantics —
146	  no concurrent request can observe an intermediate state, and on
147	  automatic streams each element sees the watermark left by the
148	  previous one;
149	* the first event-id conflict or unknown lookup key aborts the batch and
150	  rolls back every state the earlier elements touched (aggregates, dedup
151	  records, watermark, finalized results, joined groups and change
152	  sequence), so a failed batch leaves the stream exactly as before and
153	  does not occupy its identifier; too-late drops and exact duplicates
154	  remain successful outcomes;
155	* a successful batch is remembered together with its request and full
156	  response. Within the retention a retry carrying the same field values
157	  in the same event order replays the stored response without writing
158	  again (and without refreshing the retention order), while the same
159	  ``batch_id`` with different content raises BatchIdConflictError. Only
160	  the newest ``batch_retention`` records are kept; evicted identifiers
161	  may be reused, and concurrent submissions of one identifier commit at
162	  most once.
163	
164	Instances with at least one batch-enabled stream export snapshots as
165	``format_version`` 4, which always carries the ``tables`` array and, on
166	enabled streams, ``batch_retention`` plus the retained batch records in
167	commit order. Restore validates the records strictly (identifier
168	uniqueness, the retention cap, and the request/response shapes against
169	the stream's features) and publishes them so replay and eviction behave
170	exactly as on the uninterrupted instance. Older document versions
171	restore as before.
172	
173	Dimension tables may optionally be declared event-time versioned by
174	passing ``event_time_versioned: true`` at creation time (echoed in the
175	create response; without it the table keeps the current-value overwrite
176	semantics above and every public shape is unchanged). A versioned table
177	receives rows of ``key``/``label``/``effective_from_ms`` through the
178	same row entry point: each version of a key is effective from its
179	``effective_from_ms`` until the key's next version, writes may arrive
180	out of order, a first write or a new effective time reports
181	``changed: true``, an identical retry reports ``changed: false``, and
182	an existing ``(key, effective_from_ms)`` point resubmitted with a
183	different label raises DimensionVersionConflictError and leaves the
184	history untouched. A stream whose ``lookup_table`` is versioned
185	resolves every event's label as the newest version with
186	``effective_from_ms <= timestamp_ms`` — late-arriving or backfilled
187	history therefore only affects events whose own event time it precedes
188	and never recomputes already received events; an unknown key or an
189	event time before the key's first version raises
190	LookupVersionNotFoundError with all state untouched. Dedup, lateness,
191	windowing, watermarks, change-feed sequence numbers and batch
192	atomicity (a missing version anywhere rolls the whole batch back) are
193	exactly as on current-value joins.
194	
195	Instances with at least one versioned table export snapshots as
196	``format_version`` 5, which always carries the ``tables`` array; each
197	table object records its mode, and versioned tables export their rows
198	as ``versions`` strictly ordered by ``key`` then ``effective_from_ms``.
199	Restore stays compatible with versions 1 to 4 and validates version 5
200	strictly (mode field combinations, duplicate or out-of-order versions,
201	invalid effective times and conflicting points all raise SnapshotError
202	without publishing partial state).
203	
204	Optional local persistence is available by pointing the
205	``STREAMMILL_STATE_FILE`` environment variable at a file path before
206	starting the HTTP server (``Service.from_state_file`` implements the
207	same startup contract in-process). Without the variable the service
208	keeps its pure in-memory behavior. With it, a missing file starts an
209	empty instance and an existing file is loaded as one snapshot document
210	under the exact restore contract above — invalid UTF-8, invalid JSON or
211	a document the restore entry point would reject (likewise an empty
212	path, a directory, or a missing/unwritable parent directory) aborts
213	startup before anything listens. Every successful state-changing
214	request (stream/table creation, row writes, events and batches,
215	watermark advances, snapshot restores) is then a single durable commit:
216	the complete post-commit snapshot is written atomically (temp file plus
217	rename, so the path only ever presents one complete snapshot) while
218	still holding the state lock, and only then is success returned.
219	Successful requests that leave the public state unchanged — too-late
220	drops, exact duplicates, identical row values, identical watermarks and
221	replays of retained batches — return their usual response without
222	touching the file, and failed requests never write either. If a persist
223	fails at runtime the in-memory state is rolled back to the pre-commit
224	snapshot, the file keeps the previous complete commit, and
225	StatePersistError is raised (HTTP 503 ``state_persist_failed``), so a
226	retry is processed exactly as if the request had never happened.
227	
228	Streams may optionally bound their simultaneously open windows by
229	passing a positive ``max_open_windows`` at creation time (echoed in the
230	create response; without it the stream behaves exactly as before). Only
231	base windows that are not yet finalized occupy slots — sliding windows
232	count separately, joined groups, finalized results and change records
233	never do:
234	
235	* single events still run the usual validation, dedup, lateness and
236	  dimension-resolution steps first; exact duplicates and too-late drops
237	  create no windows and keep their original successful outcomes. Any
238	  other event is aggregated (and, on automatic streams, the watermark
239	  advance runs) and the resulting open-window count is compared against
240	  the limit; over the limit the event is rejected with
241	  StreamBackpressuredError (HTTP 429 ``stream_backpressured``) and every
242	  state it touched — aggregates, dedup record, maximum event timestamp,
243	  watermark, finalized results, change sequence and persisted state —
244	  is rolled back;
245	* batches apply the same check per element in input order; the first
246	  element over the limit fails the whole batch with 429
247	  ``stream_backpressured``, rolls every element back atomically and
248	  does not occupy the ``batch_id``;
249	* advancing the watermark finalizes windows and frees their slots
250	  immediately, so a manual advance always relieves pressure;
251	* ``Service.pressure`` reports the configured limit, the current open
252	  base windows and the remaining slots (HTTP 404 ``stream_not_found``
253	  for unknown streams, 409 ``backpressure_not_enabled`` on streams
254	  without a limit).
255	
256	Instances with at least one backpressured stream export snapshots as
257	``format_version`` 6, which always carries the ``tables`` array and, on
258	enabled streams, ``max_open_windows``. Restore stays compatible with
259	versions 1 to 5; a version 6 document must carry the limit on at least
260	one stream (older versions must not carry it at all) and no enabled
261	stream's open base windows may exceed its limit — any violation raises
262	SnapshotError and leaves the instance empty. After a restore the
263	pressure query, slot release, batch rollback, change sequence and
264	subsequent writes behave exactly as on the uninterrupted instance, and
265	local persistence saves the configuration and state atomically.
266	"""

430	    def put_version(self, key: str, label: str, effective_from_ms: int) -> bool:
431	        """Insert one version point; return True when the history changed.
432	
433	        An identical retry of an existing point leaves the history
434	        untouched and reports no change; the same point with a different
435	        label is a conflict and also leaves the history untouched.
436	        """
437	        timeline = self.versions.setdefault(key, [])
438	        index = bisect.bisect_left(
439	            timeline, effective_from_ms, key=lambda point: point[0]
440	        )
441	        if index < len(timeline) and timeline[index][0] == effective_from_ms:
442	            if timeline[index][1] == label:
443	                return False
444	            raise DimensionVersionConflictError(
445	                f"version ({key!r}, {effective_from_ms}) already exists with a "
446	                f"different label"
447	            )
448	        timeline.insert(index, (effective_from_ms, label))
449	        return True

461	            bisect.bisect_right(timeline, timestamp_ms, key=lambda point: point[0])
462	            - 1

465	            raise LookupVersionNotFoundError(key)

507	        self.max_event_timestamp: int | None = None
508	        # window_start_ms -> [count, sum]; only non-empty windows exist.
509	        self._windows: dict[int, list] = {}
510	        self._finalized: list[dict] = []
511	        self._finalized_starts: set[int] = set()
512	        # event_id -> (timestamp_ms, value) for accepted, not yet evicted
513	        # ids; joined streams append the lookup_key to the tuple.
514	        self._dedup: dict[str, tuple] = {}
515	        # Joined streams only: window_start_ms -> (lookup_key, label) ->
516	        # [count, sum] for open windows, plus the finalized group rows in
517	        # results order (window start, lookup_key, label).
518	        self._joined_windows: dict[int, dict[tuple[str, str], list]] = {}
519	        self._joined_finalized: list[dict] = []
520	        # Change feed: the next record gets _latest_seq + 1; _changes
521	        # holds at most change_retention records, oldest first.
522	        self._latest_seq = 0
523	        self._changes: list[dict] = []
524	        # Retained batch records in commit order, at most batch_retention
525	        # of them; each is {"batch_id", "request", "response"}.
526	        self._batches: list[dict] = []

528	    @property
529	    def _step_ms(self) -> int:
530	        """Grid spacing: slide_ms for sliding streams, else window_ms."""
531	        return self.slide_ms if self.slide_ms is not None else self.window_ms
532	
533	    def _window_starts(self, timestamp_ms: int) -> list[int]:
534	        """Starts of every grid window covering ``timestamp_ms``.
535	
536	        Windows are ``[start, start + window_ms)`` with ``start`` on the
537	        grid of multiples of the step; the floor division keeps the same
538	        boundaries for negative timestamps. The list is ascending, which
539	        is also the finalization/results order.
540	        """
541	        step = self._step_ms
542	        last = (timestamp_ms // step) * step
543	        first = last - (self.window_ms - step)
544	        return list(range(first, last + 1, step))

546	    def add_event(
547	        self,
548	        timestamp_ms: int,
549	        value: float,
550	        event_id: str | None = None,
551	        lookup_key: str | None = None,
552	        label_of=None,
553	    ) -> dict:
554	        """Process one event against the pre-event watermark.
555	
556	        On automatic streams every response additionally carries the
557	        post-processing ``watermark_ms`` (``None`` until a watermark exists)
558	        and the ``finalized`` windows produced by this response; duplicate
559	        and dropped events leave the watermark untouched and finalize
560	        nothing. Accepted-event bookkeeping (maximum event timestamp plus
561	        the resulting monotone watermark advance) only runs after
562	        aggregation and dedup registration.
563	
564	        On joined streams the label for ``lookup_key`` is read through
565	        ``label_of`` after the dedup and lateness decisions but before
566	        any state mutation, so an unknown key (or, on a versioned table,
567	        a timestamp before the key's first version) raises with all
568	        state untouched. The dedup check includes the lookup key: an
569	        exact retry repeats timestamp, value and key, while the same id
570	        with a different key conflicts.
571	        """
572	        automatic = self.auto_watermark_lag_ms is not None
573	        joined = self.lookup_table is not None
574	        if self.dedup_retention_ms is not None:
575	            retained = self._dedup.get(event_id)
576	            if retained is not None:
577	                same = retained[0] == timestamp_ms and retained[1] == value
578	                if joined:
579	                    same = same and retained[2] == lookup_key
580	                if same:
581	                    outcome: dict = {"dropped": False, "duplicate": True}
582	                    if automatic:
583	                        outcome.update(watermark_ms=self.watermark, finalized=[])
584	                    return outcome
585	                raise EventIdConflictError(event_id)
586	            if self._is_too_late(timestamp_ms):
587	                # Unseen too-late ids are dropped without being remembered.
588	                outcome = {"dropped": True, "duplicate": False}
589	                if automatic:
590	                    outcome.update(watermark_ms=self.watermark, finalized=[])
591	                return outcome
592	            label = self._resolve_label(label_of, lookup_key, timestamp_ms)
593	            backup = self._pressure_backup()
594	            self._aggregate(timestamp_ms, value, lookup_key, label)
595	            self._dedup[event_id] = (
596	                (timestamp_ms, value, lookup_key)
597	                if joined
598	                else (timestamp_ms, value)
599	            )
600	            outcome = {"dropped": False, "duplicate": False}
601	        else:
602	            if self._is_too_late(timestamp_ms):
603	                outcome = {"dropped": True}
604	                if automatic:
605	                    outcome.update(watermark_ms=self.watermark, finalized=[])
606	                return outcome
607	            label = self._resolve_label(label_of, lookup_key, timestamp_ms)
608	            backup = self._pressure_backup()
609	            self._aggregate(timestamp_ms, value, lookup_key, label)
610	            outcome = {"dropped": False}
611	        if automatic:
612	            newly = self._note_accepted_event(timestamp_ms)
613	            outcome.update(watermark_ms=self.watermark, finalized=newly)
614	        self._enforce_open_window_limit(backup)
615	        return outcome

617	    def _pressure_backup(self) -> tuple | None:
618	        """Pre-mutation state for the open-window limit, when enabled."""
619	        if self.max_open_windows is None:
620	            return None
621	        return self._state_backup()
622	
623	    def _open_window_count(self) -> int:
624	        """Base windows not yet finalized; nothing else occupies slots."""
625	        return sum(
626	            1 for start in self._windows if start not in self._finalized_starts
627	        )
628	
629	    def _enforce_open_window_limit(self, backup: tuple | None) -> None:
630	        """Reject the just-processed event when it exceeds the limit.
631	
632	        The count is taken after aggregation and the automatic watermark
633	        advance, so windows the advance finalized already freed their
634	        slots. Over the limit the whole event is rolled back — aggregates,
635	        dedup record, maximum event timestamp, watermark, finalized
636	        results and change sequence — and StreamBackpressuredError is
637	        raised, leaving the stream exactly as before the event.
638	        """
639	        if backup is None:
640	            return
641	        if self._open_window_count() > self.max_open_windows:
642	            self._state_restore(backup)
643	            raise StreamBackpressuredError(
644	                f"stream {self.name!r} exceeds max_open_windows "
645	                f"{self.max_open_windows}"
646	            )

648	    def apply_batch(self, events: list[dict], label_of=None) -> list[dict]:
649	        """Apply a whole batch atomically, in input order.
650	
651	        Every element goes through the regular single-event path, so
652	        dedup, lateness, lookup, window, automatic-watermark,
653	        finalization and change-feed semantics are identical to posting
654	        the events one by one; each element observes the state left by
655	        the previous ones. The first EventIdConflictError,
656	        LookupKeyNotFoundError or StreamBackpressuredError rolls every
657	        mutation back — aggregates, dedup records, watermark, finalized
658	        results, joined groups and the change sequence — so a failed
659	        batch leaves no trace.
660	        """
661	        backup = self._state_backup()
662	        outcomes: list[dict] = []
663	        try:
664	            for event in events:
665	                outcomes.append(
666	                    self.add_event(
667	                        event["timestamp_ms"],
668	                        event["value"],
669	                        event.get("event_id"),
670	                        event.get("lookup_key"),
671	                        label_of,
672	                    )
673	                )
674	        except Exception:
675	            self._state_restore(backup)
676	            raise
677	        return outcomes

679	    def _state_backup(self) -> tuple:
680	        """Deep snapshot of every mutable structure a batch can touch."""
681	        return (
682	            self.watermark,
683	            self.max_event_timestamp,
684	            copy.deepcopy(self._windows),
685	            copy.deepcopy(self._finalized),
686	            set(self._finalized_starts),
687	            copy.deepcopy(self._dedup),
688	            copy.deepcopy(self._joined_windows),
689	            copy.deepcopy(self._joined_finalized),
690	            self._latest_seq,
691	            copy.deepcopy(self._changes),
692	        )
693	
694	    def _state_restore(self, backup: tuple) -> None:
695	        (
696	            self.watermark,
697	            self.max_event_timestamp,
698	            self._windows,
699	            self._finalized,
700	            self._finalized_starts,
701	            self._dedup,
702	            self._joined_windows,
703	            self._joined_finalized,
704	            self._latest_seq,
705	            self._changes,
706	        ) = backup

708	    def _resolve_label(self, label_of, lookup_key: str | None, timestamp_ms: int):
709	        """Read the label for a joined event, or None on plain streams.
710	
711	        The reader receives the event's own ``timestamp_ms`` so a
712	        versioned table resolves the version effective at event time; a
713	        current-value table ignores it.
714	        """
715	        if self.lookup_table is None:
716	            return None
717	        return label_of(lookup_key, timestamp_ms)
718	
719	    def _is_too_late(self, timestamp_ms: int) -> bool:
720	        return (
721	            self.watermark is not None
722	            and timestamp_ms < self.watermark - self.allowed_lateness_ms
723	        )
724	
725	    def _note_accepted_event(self, timestamp_ms: int) -> list[dict]:
726	        """Advance the max event timestamp and then the watermark."""
727	        if (
728	            self.max_event_timestamp is None
729	            or timestamp_ms > self.max_event_timestamp
730	        ):
731	            self.max_event_timestamp = timestamp_ms
732	        target = self.max_event_timestamp - self.auto_watermark_lag_ms
733	        if self.watermark is None or target > self.watermark:
734	            # Publish through the shared path so finalization and dedup
735	            # eviction behave exactly like a manual advance.
736	            return self.advance_watermark(target)
737	        return []
738	
739	    def _aggregate(
740	        self,
741	        timestamp_ms: int,
742	        value: float,
743	        lookup_key: str | None = None,
744	        label: str | None = None,
745	    ) -> None:
746	        for start in self._window_starts(timestamp_ms):
747	            bucket = self._windows.setdefault(start, [0, 0])
748	            bucket[0] += 1
749	            bucket[1] += value
750	            # Base-window upsert with the post-event aggregates; sliding
751	            # streams publish one record per window, ascending by start.
752	            self._append_change("upsert", start, bucket[0], bucket[1])
753	            if self.lookup_table is not None:
754	                groups = self._joined_windows.setdefault(start, {})
755	                group = groups.setdefault((lookup_key, label), [0, 0])
756	                group[0] += 1
757	                group[1] += value
758	
759	    def _append_change(self, kind: str, start: int, count: int, total: float) -> None:
760	        """Publish one change-feed record and trim to the retention cap.
761	
762	        Sequence numbers are handed out consecutively from 1 and never
763	        regress; trimming only drops the oldest retained records.
764	        """
765	        if self.change_retention is None:
766	            return
767	        self._latest_seq += 1
768	        self._changes.append(
769	            {
770	                "seq": self._latest_seq,
771	                "kind": kind,
772	                "window_start_ms": start,
773	                "window_end_ms": start + self.window_ms,
774	                "count": count,
775	                "sum": total,
776	            }
777	        )
778	        overflow = len(self._changes) - self.change_retention
779	        if overflow > 0:
780	            del self._changes[:overflow]
781	
782	    def advance_watermark(self, watermark_ms: int) -> list[dict]:
783	        if self.watermark is not None and watermark_ms < self.watermark:
784	            raise WatermarkRegressionError(
785	                f"watermark {watermark_ms} is below current {self.watermark}"
786	            )
787	        self.watermark = watermark_ms
788	        newly: list[dict] = []
789	        for start in sorted(self._windows):
790	            if start in self._finalized_starts:
791	                continue
792	            end = start + self.window_ms
793	            if watermark_ms >= end + self.allowed_lateness_ms:
794	                count, total = self._windows[start]
795	                newly.append(
796	                    {
797	                        "stream": self.name,
798	                        "window_start_ms": start,
799	                        "window_end_ms": end,
800	                        "count": count,
801	                        "sum": total,
802	                    }
803	                )
804	                self._finalized_starts.add(start)
805	                # The final record of a window always follows every
806	                # upsert of the triggering commit.
807	                self._append_change("final", start, count, total)
808	                if self.lookup_table is not None:
809	                    # Joined groups finalize synchronously with their window,
810	                    # ordered by (lookup_key, label) within it.
811	                    groups = self._joined_windows.pop(start, {})
812	                    for key, group_label in sorted(groups):
813	                        group_count, group_sum = groups[(key, group_label)]
814	                        self._joined_finalized.append(
815	                            {
816	                                "stream": self.name,
817	                                "window_start_ms": start,
818	                                "window_end_ms": end,
819	                                "lookup_key": key,
820	                                "label": group_label,
821	                                "count": group_count,
822	                                "sum": group_sum,
823	                            }
824	                        )
825	        self._finalized.extend(newly)
826	        if self.dedup_retention_ms is not None:
827	            horizon = watermark_ms - self.dedup_retention_ms
828	            self._dedup = {
829	                event_id: kept
830	                for event_id, kept in self._dedup.items()
831	                if kept[0] >= horizon
832	            }
833	        return newly
834	
835	    def results(self) -> list[dict]:
836	        return [dict(row) for row in self._finalized]

838	    def to_snapshot(self) -> dict:
839	        """Serialize this stream as one entry of a version-1 snapshot."""
840	        entry: dict = {
841	            "name": self.name,
842	            "window_ms": self.window_ms,
843	            "allowed_lateness_ms": self.allowed_lateness_ms,
844	            "dedup_retention_ms": self.dedup_retention_ms,
845	            "watermark_ms": self.watermark,
846	            "windows": [
847	                {
848	                    "window_start_ms": start,
849	                    "window_end_ms": start + self.window_ms,
850	                    "count": self._windows[start][0],
851	                    "sum": self._windows[start][1],
852	                }
853	                for start in sorted(self._windows)
854	                if start not in self._finalized_starts
855	            ],
856	            "finalized": sorted(
857	                (dict(row) for row in self._finalized),
858	                key=lambda row: row["window_start_ms"],
859	            ),
860	        }
861	        if self.auto_watermark_lag_ms is not None:
862	            # Automatic streams publish the pair together; manual streams
863	            # keep the historical document shape exactly.
864	            entry["auto_watermark_lag_ms"] = self.auto_watermark_lag_ms
865	            entry["max_event_timestamp_ms"] = self.max_event_timestamp
866	        if self.slide_ms is not None:
867	            # Sliding streams publish the step; documents without it
868	            # restore as tumbling streams.
869	            entry["slide_ms"] = self.slide_ms
870	        if self.lookup_table is not None:
871	            # Joined streams publish the table reference plus the grouped
872	            # state; only format_version 2 documents may carry these.
873	            entry["lookup_table"] = self.lookup_table
874	            joined_open = []
875	            for start in sorted(self._joined_windows):
876	                groups = self._joined_windows[start]
877	                for key, group_label in sorted(groups):
878	                    group_count, group_sum = groups[(key, group_label)]
879	                    joined_open.append(
880	                        {
881	                            "window_start_ms": start,
882	                            "window_end_ms": start + self.window_ms,
883	                            "lookup_key": key,
884	                            "label": group_label,
885	                            "count": group_count,
886	                            "sum": group_sum,
887	                        }
888	                    )
889	            entry["joined_windows"] = joined_open
890	            entry["joined_finalized"] = [dict(row) for row in self._joined_finalized]
891	        if self.dedup_retention_ms is not None:
892	            records = []
893	            for event_id, kept in sorted(self._dedup.items()):
894	                record = {
895	                    "event_id": event_id,
896	                    "timestamp_ms": kept[0],
897	                    "value": kept[1],
898	                }
899	                if self.lookup_table is not None:
900	                    record["lookup_key"] = kept[2]
901	                records.append(record)
902	            entry["dedup_records"] = records
903	        if self.change_retention is not None:
904	            # Change-feed streams publish the config, the cursor and the
905	            # retained records; only format_version 3 documents may carry
906	            # these.
907	            entry["change_retention"] = self.change_retention
908	            entry["latest_seq"] = self._latest_seq
909	            entry["changes"] = [dict(record) for record in self._changes]
910	        if self.batch_retention is not None:
911	            # Batch-enabled streams publish the config plus the retained
912	            # batch records in commit order; only format_version 4
913	            # documents may carry these.
914	            entry["batch_retention"] = self.batch_retention
915	            entry["batches"] = copy.deepcopy(self._batches)
916	        if self.max_open_windows is not None:
917	            # Backpressured streams publish the open-window limit; only
918	            # format_version 6 documents may carry it.
919	            entry["max_open_windows"] = self.max_open_windows
920	        return entry

922	    @classmethod
923	    def from_snapshot(
924	        cls,
925	        data: object,

928	        allow_batches: bool = False,
929	        allow_backpressure: bool = False,
930	    ) -> "_Stream":
931	        """Rebuild one stream from a snapshot entry or raise SnapshotError.
932	
933	        Every structural and semantic rule is checked and nothing is
934	        repaired: callers get a fully formed stream or nothing. Join
935	        fields (``lookup_table``, ``joined_windows``, ``joined_finalized``)
936	        are only accepted when ``table_names`` is given (a version 2
937	        document); the referenced table must be one of them. Change-feed
938	        fields (``change_retention``, ``latest_seq``, ``changes``) are
939	        only accepted when ``allow_change_feed`` is set (a version 3
940	        document). Batch fields (``batch_retention``, ``batches``) are
941	        only accepted when ``allow_batches`` is set (a version 4
942	        document). The backpressure field (``max_open_windows``) is only
943	        accepted when ``allow_backpressure`` is set (a version 6
944	        document), and the restored open base windows must not exceed it.
945	        """
946	        if not isinstance(data, dict):
947	            raise SnapshotError("stream entry must be an object")

949	            "name",
950	            "window_ms",
951	            "allowed_lateness_ms",
952	            "dedup_retention_ms",
953	            "watermark_ms",
954	            "windows",
955	            "finalized",
956	            "dedup_records",
957	            "auto_watermark_lag_ms",
958	            "max_event_timestamp_ms",
959	            "slide_ms",
960	        }
961	        if table_names is not None:
962	            allowed |= {"lookup_table", "joined_windows", "joined_finalized"}
963	        if allow_change_feed:
964	            allowed |= {"change_retention", "latest_seq", "changes"}
965	        if allow_batches:
966	            allowed |= {"batch_retention", "batches"}
967	        if allow_backpressure:
968	            allowed |= {"max_open_windows"}
969	        extra = sorted(set(data) - allowed)
970	        if extra:
971	            raise SnapshotError(f"stream entry has unexpected field: {extra[0]}")
972	        required = {
973	            "name",
974	            "window_ms",
975	            "allowed_lateness_ms",
976	            "dedup_retention_ms",
977	            "watermark_ms",
978	            "windows",
979	            "finalized",
980	        }
981	        missing = sorted(required - set(data))
982	        if missing:
983	            raise SnapshotError(f"stream entry missing required field: {missing[0]}")
984	
985	        # The automatic-watermark pair must appear together; a document
986	        # without it restores as a manual stream.
987	        has_lag = "auto_watermark_lag_ms" in data
988	        has_max = "max_event_timestamp_ms" in data
989	        if has_lag != has_max:
990	            raise SnapshotError(
991	                f"stream entry automatic-watermark fields must appear together: "
992	                f"auto_watermark_lag_ms and max_event_timestamp_ms"
993	            )
994	        auto_lag = data.get("auto_watermark_lag_ms") if has_lag else None
995	        if has_lag and (not _is_int(auto_lag) or auto_lag < 0):
996	            raise SnapshotError(
997	                f"stream {data.get('name')!r}: auto_watermark_lag_ms must be a "
998	                f"non-negative integer"
999	            )
1000	        max_event_timestamp = data.get("max_event_timestamp_ms") if has_max else None
1001	        if has_max and max_event_timestamp is not None and not _is_int(
1002	            max_event_timestamp
1003	        ):
1004	            raise SnapshotError(
1005	                f"stream {data.get('name')!r}: max_event_timestamp_ms must be an "
1006	                f"integer or null"
1007	            )
1008	
1009	        name = data.get("name")
1010	        if not isinstance(name, str) or not name:
1011	            raise SnapshotError("stream name must be a non-empty string")
1012	        window_ms = data.get("window_ms")
1013	        if not _is_int(window_ms) or window_ms <= 0:
1014	            raise SnapshotError(f"stream {name!r}: window_ms must be a positive integer")
1015	        slide_ms = data.get("slide_ms") if "slide_ms" in data else None
1016	        if "slide_ms" in data and (
1017	            not _is_int(slide_ms)
1018	            or slide_ms <= 0
1019	            or slide_ms > window_ms
1020	            or window_ms % slide_ms != 0
1021	        ):
1022	            raise SnapshotError(
1023	                f"stream {name!r}: slide_ms must be a positive integer no larger "
1024	                f"than window_ms that evenly divides it"
1025	            )
1026	        allowed_lateness_ms = data.get("allowed_lateness_ms")
1027	        if not _is_int(allowed_lateness_ms) or allowed_lateness_ms < 0:
1028	            raise SnapshotError(
1029	                f"stream {name!r}: allowed_lateness_ms must be a non-negative integer"
1030	            )
1031	        retention = data.get("dedup_retention_ms")
1032	        if retention is not None and (not _is_int(retention) or retention <= 0):
1033	            raise SnapshotError(
1034	                f"stream {name!r}: dedup_retention_ms must be a positive integer"
1035	            )
1036	        if retention is not None and retention < allowed_lateness_ms:
1037	            raise SnapshotError(
1038	                f"stream {name!r}: dedup_retention_ms must be at least allowed_lateness_ms"
1039	            )
1040	        watermark = data.get("watermark_ms")
1041	        if watermark is not None and not _is_int(watermark):
1042	            raise SnapshotError(f"stream {name!r}: watermark_ms must be an integer or null")
1043	        if max_event_timestamp is not None and watermark is None:
1044	            raise SnapshotError(
1045	                f"stream {name!r}: non-null max_event_timestamp_ms requires a "
1046	                f"non-null watermark"
1047	            )
1048	
1049	        lookup_table = data.get("lookup_table")
1050	        if "lookup_table" in data:
1051	            if not isinstance(lookup_table, str) or not lookup_table:
1052	                raise SnapshotError(
1053	                    f"stream {name!r}: lookup_table must be a non-empty string"
1054	                )
1055	            if lookup_table not in table_names:
1056	                raise SnapshotError(

1404	    @classmethod
1405	    def _load_joined_state(
1406	        cls, stream: "_Stream", data: dict, name: str, window_ms: int
1407	    ) -> None:
1408	        """Load joined groups and check them against the base windows.
1409	
1410	        The joined groups must partition the plain window aggregates
1411	        exactly: every open or finalized base window has groups, and the
1412	        per-window group counts and sums add up to the base totals.
1413	        """
1414	        open_rows = cls._parse_joined_list(
1415	            data["joined_windows"],
1416	            name,
1417	            window_ms,
1418	            "joined_windows",
1419	            with_stream=False,
1420	            step_ms=stream._step_ms,
1421	        )
1422	        for row in open_rows:
1423	            start = row["window_start_ms"]
1424	            groups = stream._joined_windows.setdefault(start, {})
1425	            groups[(row["lookup_key"], row["label"])] = [row["count"], row["sum"]]
1426	
1427	        finalized_rows = cls._parse_joined_list(
1428	            data["joined_finalized"],
1429	            name,
1430	            window_ms,
1431	            "joined_finalized",
1432	            with_stream=True,
1433	            step_ms=stream._step_ms,
1434	        )
1435	        for row in finalized_rows:
1436	            if row["stream"] != name:
1437	                raise SnapshotError(
1438	                    f"stream {name!r}: joined_finalized row labels stream "
1439	                    f"{row['stream']!r}"
1440	                )
1441	            stream._joined_finalized.append(dict(row))
1442	
1443	        if set(stream._joined_windows) != set(stream._windows):
1444	            raise SnapshotError(
1445	                f"stream {name!r}: joined_windows do not match the open windows"
1446	            )
1447	        for start, groups in stream._joined_windows.items():
1448	            cls._check_group_totals(
1449	                name,
1450	                start,
1451	                sum(group[0] for group in groups.values()),
1452	                sum(group[1] for group in groups.values()),
1453	                stream._windows[start],
1454	            )
1455	
1456	        finalized_by_start = {
1457	            row["window_start_ms"]: row for row in stream._finalized
1458	        }
1459	        joined_finalized_starts = {
1460	            row["window_start_ms"] for row in stream._joined_finalized
1461	        }
1462	        if joined_finalized_starts != stream._finalized_starts:
1463	            raise SnapshotError(

1465	                f"windows"
1466	            )

1468	        for row in stream._joined_finalized:

1470	        for start, rows in grouped.items():
1471	            base = finalized_by_start[start]

1473	                name,
1474	                start,

1476	                sum(row["sum"] for row in rows),
1477	                (base["count"], base["sum"]),
1478	            )

1514	            if missing:

1608	                )

1610	            extra = sorted(set(raw) - fields)
1611	            if extra:
1612	                raise SnapshotError(

1614	                    f"{extra[0]}"
1615	                )
